answer: In PoA, an agent identity is issued only after remote attestation verifies the enclave’s MRENCLAVE—the measurement of its initial code—and binds its public key to a hardware-protected key. A copied VM cannot forge that attestation or export the key, so duplicating an identity requires provisioning another genuine TEE on physical silicon, not snapshotting software. This anchor raises Sybil costs; nadir-level trust still depends on vendor roots, while the vine of identities remains auditable.
